title: What Is It Made Of?
question: Why are spoons made of metal and windows made of glass?
steps: The right material for the job

steps.title: Things are made of materials
steps.text: Everything around you is made of materials. Wood, metal, plastic, glass, rubber and fabric are all materials. A table can be made of wood, and a key is made of metal.
steps.try: Press a material button to pick up that sample.
steps.see: Each sample looks and feels different. The way a material looks and acts is called its properties.

steps.title: Hard or soft?
steps.text: A hard material keeps its shape when you press it. A soft material squashes. Let's test each sample with a press.
steps.try: Press the Press button and watch the samples.
steps.see: Rubber and fabric squash down, then spring back up. Wood, metal, plastic and glass do not change shape: they are hard.

steps.title: Bendy or stiff?
steps.text: A bendy material can bend without breaking. A stiff material does not bend. Now each sample lies across two blocks and gets a push in the middle.
steps.try: Press Push and watch which samples bend.
steps.see: Rubber, fabric and the thin plastic bend. These thick pieces of wood, metal and glass stay straight. Glass is stiff, and it breaks if you bend it too hard.

steps.title: Waterproof or soaks it up?
steps.text: A waterproof material does not let water in. Some materials soak water up, like a sponge. Each sample gets one drop of water.
steps.see: The drops stay on top of metal, plastic, glass and rubber: they are waterproof. Fabric soaks its drop right up. Wood soaks up a little, slowly.

steps.title: Can you see through it?
steps.text: A see-through material lets light pass through it. Most materials block light. Now the samples stand up, and a torch shines at each one.
steps.try: Turn the Torches on and off.
steps.see: Only the light that shines at the glass reaches the wall. The other samples block the light, so you cannot see through them.

steps.title: The right material for the job
steps.text: We choose a material because of its properties. An umbrella must be waterproof and light. A window must be see-through. A spoon must be hard and stiff.
steps.try: Pick a job, then pick a material, and see if it works.
steps.see: A material can be great for one job and bad for another. Glass makes a great window but a bad umbrella. Some jobs have more than one good material.

quiz.why: Light passes through glass, so we can see through it. That is why windows are made of glass.

quiz.q: Why is a towel made of fabric?
quiz.why: Fabric soaks up water. A towel needs to soak up the water on your skin.

quiz.q: Which is the best material for a spoon?
quiz.why: Metal is hard, stiff and waterproof, so a metal spoon holds soup and does not bend.
